stories.title: Kiosk GPU-raster fix -- drop --enable-gpu-rasterization to kill the freeze class
acceptance: [Atlas RCA #1 -- design-gate] in the eclipse-dashboard chromium ExecStart (deploy/deploy-pi.sh kiosk unit) remove --enable-gpu-rasterization and use software compositing (--disable-gpu-rasterization). The dashboard is a simple 2D card UI that does not need GPU rasterization; this removes the chromium GPU command-buffer hot-loop (AllocateRingBuffer kFatalFailure, ~6M errors/boot, ~500/sec, no crash/recovery) that froze the UI. RCA: offices/architect/findings/2026-08-02-pi-ui-freeze-chromium-gpu-command-buffer-hotloop.md
doubles as the hypothesis test: with GPU raster off, the freeze must NOT reproduce under sustained carousel navigation
the change installs via the existing cmp-guarded kiosk-unit step + daemon-reload; test/verification proves the deployed unit no longer passes --enable-gpu-rasterization; ruff/lint clean in-loop

validationCriteria.action: on the Pi under sustained carousel navigation for several minutes, then `journalctl -u eclipse-dashboard | grep -c AllocateRingBuffer`
validationCriteria.outcome: count stays ~0, chromium CPU stays low, display never freezes

conditionalOutcomes: if GPU-raster-off alone does NOT eliminate the freeze, STOP and escalate to Atlas -- fix-selection (raster vs cma vs animations) is a hypothesis; do not stack blind changes
stories.goal: As the operator, I want the Pi dashboard to never freeze under sustained use, so the display stays live during a drive instead of wedging silently.

stories.title: Kiosk watchdog -- auto-restart eclipse-dashboard when the renderer wedges
acceptance: [Atlas RCA #2] add a watchdog that detects a wedged renderer (e.g. AllocateRingBuffer error-rate spike, or a CPU-pegged chromium with no state-file-driven repaint) and restarts eclipse-dashboard to restore a fresh GPU context (the proven live mitigation)

conservative trigger: restart only on a genuine wedge, never flap under normal operation; log every restart so recurring wedges stay visible (defense-in-depth behind US-522, must not mask a still-present freeze class)
test proves the watchdog triggers a restart on a simulated wedge and no-ops under healthy operation; ruff clean in-loop

validationCriteria.action: simulate/observe a renderer wedge on the Pi
validationCriteria.outcome: eclipse-dashboard is auto-restarted and the display recovers with no human intervention; the restart is logged

conditionalOutcomes: watchdog is defense-in-depth, NOT the primary fix (US-522). It must surface recurring wedges, not silence them.
stories.goal: As the operator, I want the kiosk to recover itself if the renderer ever wedges, so the display never stays silently frozen (honest-instrument).

stories.title: Raise Pi GPU CMA to 256M -- headroom complementing the raster fix
acceptance: [Atlas RCA #4 -- optional headroom, complements US-522, NOT a standalone fix] raise the Pi CMA pool to cma=256M (boot cmdline/config). Box-config change: confirm the mechanism (config.txt/cmdline.txt on the Pi boot partition) and whether deploy-pi.sh can write it within scope
verify post-boot CmaTotal reflects the raise (was 65536 kB)

validationCriteria.outcome: CmaTotal ~262144 kB (256 MiB), up from 65536 kB

conditionalOutcomes: if the boot-config change is outside Ralph's deploy write-scope (bootloader/ownership), emit a one-line CIO ops instruction instead of forcing it into the deploy script -- do not half-apply
stories.goal: As the operator, I want more GPU command-buffer headroom on the Pi, so the compositor has margin under sustained animated use.

stories.title: Splash render fix -- boot splash visibility + shutdown-splash 401 route
acceptance: investigate + fix the CIO-reported missing boot AND shutdown splash on V0.29.24 (bench, post-reboot). PM evidence (curl 127.0.0.1:9899): 401 on bare routes /boot /boot.html /dashboard /shutdown but 200 on / and /shutdown.html. Determine what URL each splash unit loads and why the bare routes 401 -- US-501's _injectHtml change in states_http_server.py is the prime suspect; also check any SSOT-token gate

boot splash: confirm it renders visibly instead of flashing sub-second before its JS window.close() at HEALTHY_YIELD (US-494 Pi-core-up readiness may fire too fast). If too fast, add a minimum-visible-duration floor so the brand splash is actually seen
shutdown splash: ensure the grace unit loads a 200 route (/shutdown.html) not a 401 (/shutdown), so the reverse splash renders on a real shutdown
honest-instrument: the splash reflects real boot/shutdown state, never a fabricated 'ready'; test proves the routes the splash units load return 200; ruff clean

validationCriteria.action: reboot the Pi and observe the boot splash; then trigger a shutdown and observe the shutdown splash
validationCriteria.outcome: boot splash is visibly shown then hands off to the dashboard; shutdown reverse splash renders on shutdown

conditionalOutcomes: [Atlas read] if the 401 on bare routes is by-design (only *.html served) and both splash units already load *.html, the fix narrows to boot-splash visibility timing only -- confirm with Atlas before touching the route/auth layer
stories.goal: As the operator, I want to see the boot and shutdown splash, so the Pi shows an honest brand + boot/shutdown state instead of a blank hand-off.

stories.title: US-504a production drain-event writer (battery_health_log grows again)
acceptance: [CARRIED from Sprint 69 / BL-028] build the PRODUCTION drain-event writer. No production caller in src/ has written battery_health_log since US-216 auto-open was retired (US-442/TD-058). BatteryHealthRecorder.startDrainEvent/endDrainEvent already write the columns correctly -- wire a production caller

[SEAM] PowerMonitor.onTransition is the registration point; PowerMonitor already receives GPIO6 truth via the US-502 _PowerSourceUiBridge sink. Read the UPS LATE-BOUND at transition time, not captured at construction (US-501/502/503 boot-order trap)

on a real AC->BATTERY transition open a drain row with a REAL start_vcell_v + start_soc_pct from the MAX17048; on BATTERY->AC or cutoff shutdown close it with real end_vcell_v/end_soc_pct + runtime_seconds. Honest-instrument: an unreadable gauge writes NULL, never a guessed number (reuse readCalibratedRegisterSocPct + its cold-start window)

[ORPHAN POLICY -- Atlas ruling, option C] open-at-loss + close-at-restore-or-shutdown, ShutdownSequencer close PRIMARY + boot reaper BACKSTOP. Spool's depth gate disqualifies option B (single-INSERT-at-close loses the run-to-cutoff drain on a hard crash) and demotes the reaper to hygiene-only. CONFIRM A-vs-C with Atlas at PRD review

[LOAD-BEARING TRAP] the boot reaper MUST NOT close orphans via endDrainEvent (it computes runtime_seconds from the timestamp delta -> across a reboot manufactures a multi-hour runtime that clears the gate + poisons the median). The reaper stamps end_timestamp and leaves runtime_seconds NULL so the row can never qualify
test proves: a production AC<->battery transition writes real vcell/soc; a cutoff-shutdown drain is closed by the sequencer; an orphaned drain is reaped with runtime_seconds NULL; ruff clean

validationCriteria.action: on the Pi force an AC->battery->AC transition (or bench harness) and query battery_health_log
validationCriteria.outcome: a new row with real start/end vcell + soc + runtime_seconds; an interrupted drain leaves an orphan with runtime_seconds NULL, never a fabricated runtime

conditionalOutcomes: gated on Atlas's orphan-policy A-vs-C confirm (Spool's depth-gate ruling already landed, narrowing to A vs C; Ralph recommends C). The depth-gate qualifying values ride US-527.
stories.goal: As the operator, I want battery_health_log to gain real rows from actual drains, so the Health verdict can leave 'unknown' honestly.

stories.title: US-504b verdict band-remap to the depth gate (degraded/replace reachable)
acceptance: [TD-074 / Spool depth-gate ruling c72677e + 429a3ed] US-504b shipped against the retired runtime_seconds>=600 gate, which sat above the 582s good/degraded boundary -> degraded/replace unreachable, verdict fails toward reassurance. Remap the qualifying gate + bands in verdictForMedianRuntime() to Spool's DEPTH gate: qualifying = end_vcell_v <= [EXACT:3.50] V AND a [EXACT:60] s minimum floor. Pull the exact good/degraded/replace depth-band thresholds from Spool's landed ruling (429a3ed)
[EXACT] values are load-bearing -- flag Spool before any drift (review-stories gate)

rides WITH US-526 (the writer that produces depth-gated rows). Latent today (no writer + 90-day staleness override -> card correctly reads unknown), so these must land together to avoid a verdict that silently cannot degrade
test proves degraded + replace are reachable through the pipeline with seeded depth-gated rows; ruff clean

validationCriteria.action: seed battery_health_log rows spanning good/degraded/replace depth bands and read the verdict
validationCriteria.outcome: verdict correctly returns degraded and replace, not only good/unknown

conditionalOutcomes: confirm exact depth-band thresholds against Spool's ruling (offices/tuner ... us504 gate ruling / 429a3ed) before implementing -- [EXACT] values.
stories.goal: As the operator, I want the battery Health verdict to actually report degraded/replace, so it fails toward honesty instead of only ever showing good/unknown.

stories.title: I-041 fix -- system_status_emitter exact-shape tests + pin lastDrive always-present
acceptance: [I-041] US-505 added drive.lastDrive to buildSystemStatusState but did not update tests/pi/splash/test_system_status_emitter.py -- 2 exact-shape tests red on the branch (test_buildSystemStatusState_a3Schema_hasExactShape, test_emitter_writesSystemStatusFile_andComputesStale). Add 'lastDrive': None to the two expected drive dicts (~lines 64, 295). Production behaviour is correct per US-505; only the expectations are stale

pin lastDrive as ALWAYS-PRESENT (US-505 makes it deliberately always a key, null when unknown, so a renderer cannot fall through to a wrong branch) -- assert presence explicitly, not just absorb the key
full tests/pi/splash green; ruff clean

validationCriteria.outcome: both previously-red exact-shape tests pass; lastDrive asserted always-present

stories.goal: As a maintainer, I want the system-status exact-shape guard green and the lastDrive contract pinned, so the schema stays honest.
